messages.subject: MML in 3PL
parts:
Hi Phil

First thanks a lot for writing mirt ! and your availability to answer our questions!!. It is terrific help !

I am using mirt package and trying to mimic an analysis done on Bilog-MG of dataset on educational assessment using 3PL (Brazilian SAEB that is equivalent of US NAEP) .
I calibrated item parameters with 3 ways:

A. Dafault with priors for parameters specified

model <- mirt.model("F1 = 1-45
PRIOR = (1-45, a1, lnorm, 0, 0.5),
(1-45, d, norm, 0, 1.13),
(1-45, g, norm, -1.516347, 0.5)”)

ch3p1 <- mirt(score_ch, TOL = .001,
model = model, itemtype="3PL”)

B. In the database of response vectors I have the students proficiency already calculated with BILOG.
So I calculated the sample mean and standard deviation of their theta and provided to mirt in GroupPars MEAN_1 (M=.59) and COV_1(SD=1.41) and let estimate = FALSE.

ch3p2 <- mirt(score_ch, TOL = .001,
model = model, itemtype="3PL", pars = start_values )

C. same as A but with empiricalhist = TRUE

ch3p3 <- mirt(score_ch, TOL = .001,
model = model, itemtype="3PL", empiricalhist = TRUE)

In all these 3 situations item parameters differ . I expect that because i am using different ways to center the scale. My questions are:

1. In A the provided M and SD are used as parameters of the prior of subject abilities in phase 1 of item calibration of MML so as to center the scale in this new M and SD (and not 0 and 1). If so
can I assume that item parameters are scaled relative to this distribution with this M and SD?

2. Can we recover the points and weights of the posterior distribution. In case in B If I calculate the mean/SD of this distribution would that be the M/SD I specified ?

3. If I use empiricalhist = TRUE will it recover the M and SD I had specified in B? (Can I recover M and SD for the empirical dist ?). Should the item parameters of run C be equal to run B ?


Thanks a lot again for your terrific work

Best

Ricardo Primi
Universidade São Francisco/ Campinas, SP, Brazil

On Wed, Apr 19, 2017 at 3:22 PM, Ricardo Primi <rpr...@mac.com> wrote:
Hi Phil

First thanks a lot for writing mirt ! and your availability to answer our questions!!. It is terrific help !
Anytime. I just hope it helps improve the quality of IRT research in the community.

I am using mirt package and trying to mimic an analysis done on Bilog-MG of dataset on educational assessment using 3PL (Brazilian SAEB that is equivalent of US NAEP) .
I calibrated item parameters with 3 ways:

A. Dafault with priors for parameters specified

        model <- mirt.model("F1 = 1-45
           PRIOR = (1-45, a1, lnorm, 0, 0.5),
                   (1-45, d, norm, 0, 1.13),
                   (1-45, g, norm, -1.516347, 0.5)”)

 ch3p1 <- mirt(score_ch, TOL = .001,
        model = model, itemtype="3PL”)

B. In the database of response vectors I have the students proficiency already calculated with BILOG.
So I calculated the sample  mean and standard deviation of their theta and provided to mirt in GroupPars MEAN_1 (M=.59) and COV_1(SD=1.41) and let estimate = FALSE.

 ch3p2 <- mirt(score_ch, TOL = .001,
        model = model, itemtype="3PL", pars = start_values )

C. same as A but with empiricalhist = TRUE

 ch3p3 <- mirt(score_ch, TOL = .001,
        model = model, itemtype="3PL",  empiricalhist = TRUE)

In all these 3 situations item parameters differ . I expect that because i am using different ways to center the scale. My questions are:

1. In A the provided M and SD are used as parameters of the prior of subject abilities in phase 1 of item calibration of MML so as to center the scale in this new M and SD (and not 0 and 1). If so
can I assume that item parameters are scaled relative to this distribution with this M and SD?
This seems like a 2-step ad-hoc process, but yes what you are trying to accomplish sounds roughly correct. I'm not sure I understand why exactly, but that's another issue.....
2. Can we recover the points and weights of the posterior distribution. In case in B If I calculate the mean/SD of this distribution would that be the M/SD I specified ?

No. The posterior deviation of the individual response patterns != the population distribution. Even with plausible value imputation this often fails (though is slightly better). It's always better to estimate these parameters concurrently if possible.
3. If I use empiricalhist = TRUE will it recover the M and SD I had specified in B? (Can I recover M and SD for the empirical dist ?). Should the item parameters of run C be equal to run B ?

The empirical histogram approach unfortunately loses all information about the scale of the distribution because it is entirely based on the table of expected counts. So, the N(0,1) assumption is not assumed or implied, though imposing any particular scaling appears difficult at the moment. It's mainly used as an exploratory tool (and even then, it has other issues.....I'll likely write a paper on this sometime). HTH.

Thanks a lot again for your terrific work

Best

Ricardo Primi
Universidade São Francisco/ Campinas, SP, Brazil
